title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Broncos
headline: Mason Rudolph drew heavy praise after starting the 27-5 win over Denver on a short week. McCarthy never addressed Aaron Rodgers' absence or what Rudolph's role looks like going forward.
summary: McCarthy said the win showed a lot about the team and credited a leadership council meeting for the urgency the players played with. He singled out T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward as examples of that leadership, and the defense set the tone early. He called the game old-fashioned, downhill football built on fundamentals, pad level and energy, and he said the team can build on it. Mason Rudolph was described as outstanding. He handled a very short week, stayed late for extra prep, and was plugged in on in-game adjustments, including the empty pressure Denver showed on first down in the third quarter. McCarthy said the offensive line and running backs did well in the run game and that the coaches communicated the adjustments well. He said Rudolph has grown on him since the spring, bought into the quarterback room's process, and has a phenomenal opportunity, and he hopes the team can build on it. McCarthy also said he is still the offensive play caller and that his involvement with the defense and the split of job responsibilities will be looked at in the offseason. He brushed off outside criticism of the team's turmoil, saying his focus was on winning, and called it a hard travel week on a short turnaround.

signals.claim: Rudolph started at quarterback on a short week, and the staff plans to build on his performance.
signals.note: Rudolph played well enough to earn strong praise and a 'phenomenal opportunity' label, which helps his case for continued QB1 snaps, though McCarthy gave no explicit commitment.

topics.detail: McCarthy credited the leadership council meeting, led by players like T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward, for the urgency. He called the win old-fashioned, black-and-blue football built on fundamentals and tenacity.

McCarthy praised the offensive line and running backs in the run game. He said the team adjusted to Denver's empty pressure on first down in the third quarter, and that communication between series was key.
McCarthy said he remains the offensive play caller and has not spent enough time with the defense. He said job responsibilities will be reviewed in the offseason.
McCarthy declined to react to outside comments about the team's turmoil. He said he is focused on winning and that the week was hard, with a short turnaround and travel.
